subtopic: KV cache OOM / Diagnosis and mitigations
learningObjective: Diagnose KV cache OOM under long-context multi-tenant serving and identify effective mitigations.
stem: A vLLM deployment on an 80GB GPU running Llama-3-70B (with GQA, 8 KV heads) is throwing frequent 'KV cache full' preemptions. Prompt/output stats and observed metrics: (Select all mitigations that would concretely reduce OOM/preemption rates.)
profileData:
Model: Llama-3-70B, GQA (H_kv=8, d=128, L=80), FP16 KV.
  Per-token KV: 2 * 80 * 8 * 128 * 2 B = 320 KB.
  Deployment: TP=8 across 8 x H100 80GB (so per-GPU KV budget ≈ (80GB - weights_per_GPU - workspace) / 8 shard).
  Actually TP-8 means KV cache is also sharded (H_kv=8 goes to 1 KV head per GPU) → per-GPU per-token KV ≈ 40 KB.
  Workload: 4K-token prompts, 500-token outputs on average; target concurrent batch = 128.
  Observed: KV usage per GPU peaks at 99%, preemption rate 30%, tail TTFT p99 = 5x p50.

options.text: Switch from TP=8 to PP=8: pipeline parallelism replicates KV cache across all pipeline stages (each stage stores the whole per-request KV), providing 8x more KV capacity per pipeline stage.
Enable INT8 or FP8 KV cache: cuts per-token KV bytes ~2x, roughly doubling concurrent batch capacity at the cost of small accuracy loss.
Reduce max_concurrent_batch (batch admission cap) so that KV pressure doesn't reach 99%: this trades peak throughput for lower preemption / better tail TTFT.
Enable prefix caching if requests share long system prompts: shared prefill KV is reused across requests, cutting effective per-request KV cost for repeated prefixes.

explanation: Options B, C, D are correct; option A is incorrect. A (Wrong): PP shards layers (each stage stores its layers' KV), it does not replicate. B (Correct): KV quant is the direct capacity lever. C (Correct): admission control trades throughput for stability. D (Correct): prefix caching reduces effective per-request KV. General context: In fact PP typically stores L/P layers' worth of KV per stage instead of L/T rows in TP.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: PP shards layers (each stage stores its layers' KV), it does not replicate.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: KV quant is the direct capacity lever.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: admission control trades throughput for stability.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: prefix caching reduces effective per-request KV.

assumptions: Prefix caching is enabled and workload has shared prefixes.
nonImplications: Does not imply INT8 KV is quality-neutral.
Does not imply admission control is preferable to horizontal scaling; both are valid.
